classification.difficultyReason: Find an intersection, prove that a parameterised family retains that point, and select its member through another given point.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the coordinates of the point $M$ where $x+2y-6=0$ and $3x-2y-6=0$ meet.

answer.worked:
Adding the two equations eliminates $y$:
$$\begin{align*}4x-12&=0\\4x&=12\\x&=3.\end{align*}$$
Substituting into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}3+2y-6&=0\\2y&=3\\y&=\frac32.\end{align*}$$
Thus $M=\left(3,\dfrac32\right)$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that the new line $(x+2y-6)+k(3x-2y-6)=0$ always passes through $M$, regardless of the value of $k$.

answer.short: At $M$, both bracketed expressions are zero, so the equation becomes $0+k(0)=0$ for every $k$.
answer.worked:
Substitute $M=\left(3,\dfrac32\right)$ into the left-hand side:
$$\begin{align*}(x+2y-6)+k(3x-2y-6)&=\left(3+2\cdot\frac32-6\right)+k\left(9-2\cdot\frac32-6\right)\\(x+2y-6)+k(3x-2y-6)&=0+k(0)\\(x+2y-6)+k(3x-2y-6)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $M$ lies on the line for every value of $k$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Hence find the equation of the line $PM$ where $P=(2,-1)$.

answer.short:
$5x-2y-12=0$.

Substitute $P$ into the family to obtain $k=3$.
answer.worked:
For the line to pass through $P=(2,-1)$:
$$\begin{align*}(2+2(-1)-6)+k(3(2)-2(-1)-6)&=0\\-6+2k&=0\\2k&=6\\k&=3.\end{align*}$$
By part b, this member also passes through $M$. Its equation is
$$\begin{align*}(x+2y-6)+3(3x-2y-6)&=0\\10x-4y-24&=0\\5x-2y-12&=0.\end{align*}$$
